source.title: Inference-Time Decomposition of Activations (ITDA): A Scalable Approach to Interpreting Large Language Models
source.authors: Patrick Leask; Neel Nanda; N. A. Moubayed

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates the effect of replacing model activations with SAE reconstructions on cross-entropy loss, a related measure of whether reconstruction error affects model computation. It does not compare SAE errors with random errors matched in size.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE reconstruction cross-entropy evaluations, but not random-error controls matched for size. It does not measure linear predictability of SAE errors, per-token error scaling or overlap across SAE sizes, two types of dark matter, or the effect of retaining SAE error in circuits or steering. Its comparisons of ITDA and SAE reconstruction performance do not establish the claim's error-structure findings.
record.test_reason: The study introduces ITDA, a matching-pursuit dictionary method, as a cheaper alternative to SAEs. Its only SAE-error-related result is SAEBench CE loss scores comparing ITDA reconstructions with pretrained SAE reconstructions (Fig. 7a). There is no random-error control matched in norm, so V3's pathology claim cannot be assessed. It does not measure linear predictability of SAE error, per-token error scaling, dark-matter components, error-term retention in circuits or steering, or whether dark matter shrinks with architecture. It neither tests nor relies on the dark-matter finding, and does not cite the original. The closest relation label is cites_only; strictly the study does not cite it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors present ITDA as 100x cheaper to train than SAEs, with reconstruction comparable to ReLU SAEs but worse than TopK/p-annealing SAEs, and notably worse on Gemma 2 2B. They also present ITDA dictionaries as yielding a state-of-the-art Jaccard representation-similarity measure. They draw no conclusions about the structure or function of SAE error.
record.recipe_differences: ITDA uses matching pursuit over a dictionary of sampled model activations, rather than a trained SAE encoder and decoder. The reported evaluation compares reconstruction methods and does not implement the dark-matter error analyses in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction performance differs by model: the text describes ITDAs as generally better than ReLU SAEs and worse than top-k SAEs on Pythia, but substantially worse than SAEs on Gemma 2 2B.

fits_no_version.finding: CE loss score degradation when splicing in reconstructions is similar to or slightly worse for ITDA than for SAEs on Pythia 70m/160m, and substantially worse on Gemma 2 2B. ITDA is better than ReLU SAEs but worse than TopK/p-annealing SAEs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-learned inference-time dictionaries (matching pursuit over sampled activations) reach reconstruction fidelity comparable to early ReLU SAEs, but not to modern SAE architectures.

record.problems: For the claim-relevant comparison, the supplied text gives no numerical SAE reconstruction scores outside the figure and reports no random-error control matched in size. SAE reconstruction results are compared across methods, not against the control needed to establish V3.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of SAE error from input activations: not measured.
Per-token error norm predictability across SAE sizes, failure on shared contexts, and persistence with scale: not measured.
SAE reconstruction loss versus norm-matched random errors: not measured. Only CE loss scores relative to the zero-ablation and clean baselines are reported.
Split into linear and nonlinear dark matter: not measured.
Effect of keeping or dropping the SAE error term in circuit or steering analyses: not measured.
Whether dark matter shrinks with SAE architecture or training choices: not measured. SAE architectures are compared only on CE loss score against ITDA, not on dark matter.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V3 link is wrong: a CE loss score without a norm-matched random-error comparison cannot test pathological errors. All rows compare the study's own method against SAE baselines, and the values are figure-only. The dark-matter paper (arXiv:2410.14670) is not cited in the reference list.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of input activations.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, overlap in contexts where different-sized SAEs fail, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction harms loss more than random errors matched in size; the study reports reconstruction-related loss scores but no such random-error comparison.
Whether the linear component reflects unlearned features and whether the nonlinear component is qualitatively different or resists dictionary learning.
Whether circuit or steering analyses lose behavior when the SAE error term is omitted.
Whether dark matter is mostly caused by SAE training choices and shrinks under better architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: Pythia-70m
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated cross-entropy loss with activations replaced by SAE reconstructions.

conditions.value: multiple methods are shown in Figure 7(a); individual values are not available in the supplied figure text

rows.measure: Cross-entropy loss score for SAE reconstruction, defined relative to original and zero-ablated model loss
rows.baseline: Original cross-entropy loss Horig and zero-ablated cross-entropy H0, used in the score definition (Eq. 7)
rows.note: The text says ITDA performance is generally better than ReLU SAEs and worse than top-k SAEs on Pythia models, but does not give SAE-specific values here. No comparison with random errors of matched size is reported.
rows.check: The CE loss score with SAE reconstructions on Pythia-70m has no random-error matched control, so it cannot show V3's 'worse than random' effect. The row compares the study's own method (ITDA) against pretrained SAEs from SAEBench. Values are figure-only. It should not be linked to V3.
